name: Rebuild Better Plan
description: Make project review mart maintenance bounded, incremental, resumable, and non-blocking for 2M-article projects while preserving correct active-generation reads.

userStories.title: Add bounded dirty-article batch claims
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want dirty project refresh claims to expose bounded DB-side article batches so large projects never load all dirty article ids into JavaScript.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a project refresh state service API that returns a deterministic dirty article batch for a project claim using a configurable batch size.
The batch query filters by claimed token and last completed token in the database and does not materialize every dirty article id before choosing a refresh path.
Add per-batch completion state so processed articles can be cleared while `last_completed_refresh_token` only advances when all claim work through that token is durable.
Cover one-article, exactly batch-sized, multi-batch, and large-scope cases in service tests.

userStories.title: Refresh global judgment facts by dirty article batch
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want `mart.judgment_fact` refreshes to replace only facts for dirty articles so unrelated project and article facts remain available during churn.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace the table-rebuild judgment fact refresh path with a batch refresh that deletes and reinserts rows by dirty `article_id` values only.
Deleted or stale judgments for dirty articles are removed from `mart.judgment_fact` without deleting facts for unrelated articles.
The batch refresh uses a temp or staging batch table instead of generated `IN (...)` lists for article ids.
Tests prove shared article facts still visible to unrelated projects are preserved.

userStories.title: Maintain project scope article deltas in batches
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want dirty article refreshes to update `mart.project_scope_article` first so every downstream mart uses the same project/article source of truth.
acceptanceCriteria: Refresh retained dirty articles in `mart.project_scope_article` before downstream fact and serving work so scope flags and article timestamps are current.
Added scope articles append scope rows and are included in downstream dirty-batch refresh work.
Removed scope articles delete only the affected `project_id + article_id` rows from project-scoped marts and active serving tables.
Tests cover retained metadata changes, scope add, scope remove, and preservation of unrelated projects and articles.

userStories.title: Refresh prompt answer and rollup marts by batch
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want dirty batches to refresh project answer facts and rollups so serving rows cannot diverge from supporting marts.
acceptanceCriteria: Delete and reinsert affected `project_id + article_id` rows in `mart.prompt_answer_fact` for each dirty batch.
Delete and reinsert affected `project_id + article_id` rows in `mart.review_article_rollup` for each dirty batch.
Append missing `app.review_answer_dictionary` values without resetting or renumbering existing answer ids.
Tests prove prompt answer facts, rollups, and dictionary ids stay in sync for the same dirty article set.

userStories.title: Refresh active serving generation by article batch
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want active serving rows, details, and filter members refreshed for many dirty articles in one bounded transaction so readers see internally consistent active-generation data.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `refreshProjectArticleMartsBatch(projectId, articleIds)` as the default dirty-article refresh path for active-generation serving data.
Delete and reinsert affected active-generation rows in `mart.review_article_serving`, `mart.review_article_serving_detail`, and `mart.review_article_filter_member` for the batch.
The active generation remains consistent across serving, detail, and filter-member rows after refresh.
Tests prove OLAP review filters and article review details return the refreshed active-generation data.

userStories.title: Route dirty refresh worker through batch maintenance
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the project mart refresh worker to use bounded dirty batches for normal churn so large projects never fall back to full project refreshes automatically.
acceptanceCriteria: Remove the dirty-article threshold path that routes normal churn into full refresh or large rebuild work.
The worker processes dirty articles through DB-side batches and calls the batch mart refresh path until the claim is complete.
When a project has no active serving generation, the per-article path queues bounded initial setup or guarded large rebuild work instead of calling `refreshProject(projectId)`.
ACKs are published only after all batches through the claim are durable.

userStories.title: Skip quarantined dirty articles without blocking claims
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want quarantined dirty articles isolated from healthy dirty work so one bad article cannot block a whole project refresh claim.
acceptanceCriteria: Dirty article batch selection skips quarantined articles while continuing to process non-quarantined dirty articles in the same project.
Quarantined dirty articles remain visible through quarantine state and warnings until repaired or cleared.
Project refresh state does not fail or block solely because one dirty article in the project is quarantined.
Tests cover quarantined and non-quarantined dirty articles in the same project claim.

userStories.title: Split large rebuild scope setup into resumable work
userStories.description: As an operator, I want large rebuild scope materialization to finish independently before fact phases so later phases use frozen scope rows and can resume safely.
acceptanceCriteria: Large rebuild setup builds `mart.project_scope_article` in bounded batches before judgment fact work depends on it.
Scope setup has either a first-class `project_scope_article` phase or a persisted sub-phase cursor that can resume separately from judgment fact work.
If a first-class phase is added, `ProjectMartLargeRebuildPhase`, phase order lists, read-model lists, admin/job/warnings progress code, and tests are updated together.
Tests prove scope setup resumes independently and progress does not treat partially materialized scope as the final denominator.

userStories.title: Use stored target generation for rebuild staging
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want one fixed target serving generation per large rebuild so staging writes and promotion remain consistent across restarts.
acceptanceCriteria: Initialize missing `target_generation` from the next serving generation before the first large rebuild staging write.
Carry the stored `target_generation` unchanged across phase transitions and lease resumes.
Executor SQL uses stored `target_generation` for every staging write and promotion instead of deriving `active_generation + 1` repeatedly.
Tests cover restart or lease expiry mid-phase with the same target generation preserved.

userStories.title: Make large rebuild judgment facts global-safe
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want large rebuild judgment fact batches to preserve shared global facts so unrelated projects can continue reading during rebuilds.
acceptanceCriteria: Remove project-owned `mart.judgment_fact` reset behavior from large rebuild execution.
Rebuild judgment facts in scoped article batches that delete only affected article facts and reinsert current non-deleted judgments.
Facts still visible to other projects sharing articles, prompts, models, and content settings are preserved.
Tests replay completed batches idempotently and prove unrelated project facts remain available.

userStories.title: Make rebuild dictionary maintenance append-only
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want large rebuild dictionary maintenance to avoid renumbering active answer ids so active-generation filter members remain valid while rebuilds run.
acceptanceCriteria: Large rebuild dictionary maintenance appends missing `app.review_answer_dictionary` values without resetting or renumbering existing answers, or introduces generationed dictionary state before any renumbering path is allowed.
Dictionary work is bounded enough for 2M-article projects and does not rely on one project-wide reset plus full `DISTINCT` scan.
Active `mart.review_article_filter_member` rows continue to reference valid dictionary ids throughout rebuild and cleanup lag.
Tests prove dictionary ids remain stable after incremental refresh, rebuild, promotion, and cleanup lag.

userStories.title: Split serving promotion from old-generation cleanup
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want large rebuild promotion to be a short active-generation update while old-generation cleanup runs later in bounded maintenance work.
acceptanceCriteria: Serving finalization promotes staged rows by setting `active_generation` to the stored `target_generation` only.
Old-generation cleanup is removed from inline finalization and moved into separate bounded maintenance batches behind refresh and judging work.
Promotion does not use full-table `DROP TABLE` or rewrite behavior and does not wait for cleanup to finish.
Tests prove cleanup can lag without changing active-generation review results or filter counts.

userStories.title: Add large rebuild wake budget and committed metrics
userStories.description: As an operator, I want large rebuild wake cycles to yield by wall-clock budget and expose committed phase throughput so background maintenance cannot monopolize the DuckDB queue.
acceptanceCriteria: The automatic large-rebuild heartbeat and admin run route accept and enforce a wall-clock time budget alongside `maxCycles` and `batchSize`.
Runtime diagnostics report rows/sec from committed batch row counts, batch duration, queue wait, RSS, last committed cursor, and available DuckDB temp spill measurements per phase.
Long cycles stop for budget exhaustion without marking rebuild work failed when the current committed cursor is safe to resume.
Tests cover heartbeat configuration, admin route options, cycle stop reasons, and metrics derived from committed work.

userStories.title: Read large rebuild progress from frozen scope
userStories.description: As a user, I want rebuild warnings and diagnostics to report progress against frozen scope rows so route or curated scope changes during rebuild do not corrupt progress estimates.
acceptanceCriteria: After scope setup completes, project warnings, judgment job storage projection, and admin rebuild status read progress estimates from `mart.project_scope_article` instead of live route or curated scope CTEs.
Progress read models handle the scope setup phase or sub-phase without treating partial scope as the final denominator.
Rows/minute and remaining-work displays are tied to committed cursors and phase-specific row counts.
Tests prove route or curated scope changes mid-rebuild do not change later-phase progress denominators.

userStories.title: Migrate obsolete project refresh queue callers
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want former project refresh queue callers to write dirty state or guarded large rebuild work directly so normal maintenance no longer depends on `refreshProject(projectId)`.
acceptanceCriteria: Migrate `queueProjectRefresh`, prompt-change, import-route/import-store, archive, unarchive, backfill, purge, and repair-script callers to dirty-state marking or guarded large rebuild enqueueing.
Delete obsolete project-task handling from `app.mart_refresh_queue` after callers move, while preserving judgment-article queue behavior if still needed.
Normal paths no longer call direct `refreshProject(projectId)` for project queue work.
Tests prove former project refresh triggers write dirty-state or large-rebuild work directly and no longer depend on project queue compatibility.

userStories.title: Bound archived-project cleanup and repair global facts
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want archived-project purge and delete cleanup to run in bounded work while keeping global judgment facts correct for surviving projects.
acceptanceCriteria: Archived-project mart cleanup runs in bounded batches behind active refresh and judging work rather than unbounded deletes or table rebuilds on normal paths.
Archived project deletion refreshes or detaches affected `mart.judgment_fact` ownership metadata without deleting facts still visible to non-archived projects.
Queued project refresh rows for archived or deleted projects are completed or pruned so they cannot remain stuck forever.
Tests cover archived cleanup, archived delete, global fact preservation, and queue-row pruning.

userStories.title: Validate active review reads and final gates
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I want API, OLAP, browser, and desktop review flows to keep using correct active-generation data while refresh or rebuild work is queued, running, promoted, and cleaned up.
acceptanceCriteria: API and OLAP review filters return the same active-generation results before refresh, during queued or running work, after promotion, and after cleanup.
Article review details return the same active-generation judgment labels and details across incremental refresh and large rebuild transitions.
Review warnings expose dirty counts, last processed batch time, rebuild progress, queue wait, RSS, and available spill or throughput diagnostics without blocking reads.
Manual 2M synthetic run confirms incremental dirty batch stays small, API remains responsive, restart resumes, and promotion is fast.
Manual browser and desktop reviews-page smoke confirms active data remains usable while refresh or rebuild work is queued or running.
